concerns.text: FR-005 mandates a 'single-sample t-test' to compare CNN MSE against baseline MSE. This is statistically invalid for paired regression errors. The errors for the CNN and the baseline are paired (same test instances), requiring a paired t-test (or Wilcoxon signed-rank) on the error differences, not a single-sample test on one model's error distribution. A single-sample test cannot validate the *difference* between two predictors.

SC-005 proposes validating interpretability by computing IoU between Grad-CAM heatmaps and 'manually annotated grain boundaries'. This is a circular/invalid validation: Grad-CAM highlights regions of high gradient contribution to the *prediction*, not necessarily physical boundaries. A model can correctly predict strength based on texture or grain interior features without highlighting boundaries. Validating 'boundary detection' via IoU against a ground-truth boundary map does not prove the model used those boundaries for prediction; it only proves the heatmap overlaps with boundaries. The metric conflates 'feature localization' with 'causal attribution'.

FR-009 requires extracting grain size features for every image to ensure 'comparative analysis uses the exact same instances'. This is redundant and potentially confounding. If the CNN is trained on raw images (FR-001/002) and the baseline is a 'naive statistical baseline' (constant mean, per FR-004), there is no need to extract grain size features for the baseline comparison. If the baseline is intended to be a physics-based model (as hinted in 'Methodology sketch' but contradicted by FR-004), the spec must explicitly define the baseline as a regression on grain size, not a constant mean. As written, FR-009 introduces an unnecessary feature extraction step that is not used in the defined baseline comparison (FR-004).
